publications.assertionSummary: Highlight 'A trusted neighbor': signed the 1645 petition and 'served as a witness and appraiser for other families' estates.'

incoming.explanation: Deed associates (Brackett, Rockwell) show community ties.
Serving as will witness and appraiser evidences trust.
Co-signing the 1646 meadows petition with the founding cohort is a documented act of town collective action, evidencing standing.

finding.shortLabel: Recognised standing in the Braintree community

sources.excerpt: debts due … to Peter Brackett, Joseph Adams …
sources.locator: John Gurney Senr inventory and debts, Braintree, 16 March 1663

finding.statement: John Gurney held recognised standing in the Braintree community — signing the 1645 plantation petition, serving as probate witness and inventory-taker for Gregory Baxter (1659), and appearing across a dense Braintree creditor network in his own 1663 estate accounts.

outgoing.explanation: Serving as will witness and appraiser evidences trust.

sources.excerpt: John Gurney … witnessed the will … inventory taken 7 July 1659 by John Gurney, Moses Paine, and Edmund Quinsey
sources.locator: Gregory Baxter profile, p. 138 (Suffolk Probate Records 1:323; 3:146)

finding.statement: John Gurney witnessed Gregory Baxter's Braintree will in 1659 (with Moses Payne and Richard Brackett) and helped take the estate inventory on 7 July 1659.
